recipes.name: Japanese Tamago Egg
ingredients_raw: 0.5 teaspoon vegetable oil, or more as needed

steps.text: Beat eggs thoroughly in a bowl; whisk in dashi stock, sugar, mirin, and soy sauce until sugar has dissolved. Lightly grease a tamago pan or a small nonstick skillet and heat over medium heat.
Pour a thin layer of egg mixture into the hot pan and swirl to coat the pan. Cook until egg layer is firm on the bottom but still slightly liquid on top, about 1 minute.
Then lift up one edge using a spatula and roll up the egg layer.
Push omelet roll to one side of the skillet. Oil the skillet again and pour in another thin layer of egg, lifting the first omelet roll up slightly to allow the egg to flow underneath.
Roll up the first omelet in the new layer of egg and push omelet to the edge of the skillet as before.
Repeat the process with the remaining egg mixture, oiling the pan each time if needed.
Remove rolled omelet to a serving platter and cut into 6 equal pieces to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Japanese Tamago Egg
raw_recipe.description: Tamago is a light, slightly sweet and savory Japanese rolled omelet also known as tamagoyaki — it will make a great addition to your sushi platter!

review.reviewBody: Good stuff. I personally feel that wrapping the slices with nori (seaweed used for onigiri) makes it taste better.

The Tamago pan is a must for an even omelette. They can be found in most Asian markets and on Amazon for around $20.00. The advantage to using this recipe with a rectangular pan is that the ends come out even and you get more omelette without any waste using the same pour egg mixture in the pan, flip or roll the set part of the omelette in half, add more egg mixture, wait until it sets, flip again, etc, etc until the Tamago is built as high as the pan. A nice finishing touch is to square up the rolled egg using a plastic lined sushi mat to make the Tamago square end to end. Tamago is a great sushi topping as well a welcome surprise in a bento. A light sprinkling of toasted sesame seeds makes for a complementary flavor.

I used to make these often. My chickens just started laying, so I wanted something different for breakfast. I often top w slices of avocado, for Tamago maki, and sprinkle the tamago w furikake when using avocado. So yummy!!! I’ve also made these into hand rolls. Good stuff!!! i have also ground up my dried Shiitake stems up in the grinder, stems which are often discarded by others, or used for soup, add the ground Shiitake first to the oil, then proceed w the egg rolling in the pan. I use a 8 x 8 rectangular ceramic pan for these. Oil generously. The ground Shiitake is in the center, after rolling the egg.

This recipe was amazing! I didn't have the wine necessary, so I substituted 1/2 tsp sugar and 1/2 tsp red wine vinegar thoroughly blended together. Also, being vegetarian, I had to make the Dashi stock - I boiled 2 cups of water with a sheet of dried sushinori seaweed and one Morning Star Farms veggie sausage roll, and added a teaspoon of salt. Both of the substitutes worked perfectly well!
Also, I cut a sheet of sushinori seaweed into strips and wrapped it around the egg rolls when they were cooled, like in the picture. I served them over plain white rice with spicy szechuan sauce. Delicious!

I made this several times. For me, I removed the sugar and dashi, and as the layers cooked I added very thin mushroom slices and the occasional piece of Nori.

To serve, I presented with Hot Mustard and Soy.

This is saved on my recipes and I follow it each week for my tamago fix. I substitute the dashi for chicken bone broth or chicken stock and the flavour is subtle. I also haven't found dashi in any shops near me but will give it a try if I do. My husband bought me a tamago pan and this has made it infinitely easier to make compared to the pancake pan I was using to start with so I would recommend!

After I stopped giggling at the name...tamago means egg so its titled egg egg.... hahaha.. I got to work making the dashimaki tamagoyaki. Very good recipee. I personally added a pinch of salt and used a sieve to make fluffier eggs.

I have been making these tamago for some years, calling them, in my bed and breakfast, "YouTube eggs" because I learned to make them on YouTube originally. Recently I received an induction-ready pan from Japan because my old pans were aluminum. The details in this recipe, plus the serving ideas, are very helpful. Much appreciated. From now on, I will add a little sugar, a little mirin, and serve on top of rice in the way you suggest.

You dont need to use dashi. I just used the mirin and i like my tamago sweeter so i made it 2 tables spoons. Also its nice served cold. You can keep it wrapped in cling wrap in the ref so it stays moist. Once your ready to serve it, thats the only time you slice it

Inspired by Molly Yeh this morning, I had to try this. I'm familiar with tamago from its' inclusion in sushi rolls. Don't have a rectangular skillet, resorted to non-stick aluminum. My execution was a 3, the flavor 5! Even my very discriminating spouse exclaimed "This is excellent!" The next time I make this, I'll have the ideal Japanese cast iron tamagoyaki pan to help me perfect it. Worth making if this cuisine suits you. Spoiler alert: now I'm inventorying our sushi production tools, ingredients & inspirations to make & share with family & friends. Shokuyoku ga ii!
The taste is great by itself, veggies or meat would enhance it too! Flipping/rolling will take practice to get it perfect, but taste is unaffected!
Omg delicious, I made tamago maki with avocado. Love this recipe, first time making tamago and using my special pan! My rolling leaves much to be desired though!
good!
I loved it so much!
Turned out great!
WOW- this makes eggs actually taste GOOD!
Authentic flavor. Thank you!

Very good! The only changes we made were to use chicken broth instead of dashi stock (we didn't have it and I don't eat fish) and apple cider vinegar instead of mirin since we didn't have that either. It was delicious!
I liked the recipe, but it was a bit sweeter than when I've had it before. When I make it again, I'll probably cut out the sugar by 1/3.
So yummy and easy! I used a round skillet and it worked great. Probably not as pretty, but tasted fantastic.
